messages:
nora-cs: quick flag 6 Larkly onboarding: they9re seeing a wave of 429s right after their CI-driven deploys. renewal review in 3 days so want a fast remediation.

ash-se: can you paste an example failed response (headers + request id)? helps identify if it9s preflight vs route qps.

nora-cs: pasted: status=429 body=\"rate_limited\" headers: `x-rw-rlimit: preflight=4/60`, `x-request-id: rq_z77a`, `x-client: larkly-prod`

tomo-eng: preflight=4/60 points at ephemeral token creation limits. what9s their init/refresh pattern?

nora-cs: they have a CI job that fires many short-lived containers for integration tests; each container initializes the SDK and also aggressively refreshes ephemerals on test teardown. snippet from them: ```bash
# CI matrix spawns 20 containers in parallel
# each runs
node -e "const R=require('redwood'); const c=new R.Client({key:process.env.LARK_KEY, preflight:true}); c.init().then(()=>console.log('ok'))"
# test finishes -> each container calls c.refresh() concurrently
```

ash-se: two issues: parallel init AND synchronized refresh on teardown. that refresh storm looks like a token churn pattern. short-term: ask CI to serialize refresh or reuse a token across matrix jobs, or add a tiny random jitter before refresh.

maya-ops: ops policy note: onboarding tier default preflight limiter is 5/min. we can open a short exception if CS needs time to patch. rl-bot: please create an ephemeral bypass if approved.

rl-bot: created bypass TB-9212: scope=account:larkly-prod, preflight_limit=50/min, duration=2h, expires=2030-01-01T12:00:00Z

tomo-eng: while bypass is active i'll send a short playbook: 1) consolidate token acquisition in a shared sidecar or process; 2) coalesce refreshes using a single leader; 3) add jitter on teardown so refreshes don9t align. example leader/coalesce snippet: ```js
// leader coalesce pattern (process-wide)
let tokenPromise = null;
function getEphemeral(){
  if (!tokenPromise) tokenPromise = fetchEphemeralToken().finally(()=> tokenPromise = null);
  return tokenPromise;
}
// callers await getEphemeral() instead of each calling refresh in parallel
```

ash-se: also recommend a lightweight CI change: if they must refresh on teardown, add `await sleep(random(0,3000))` before refresh and prefer a single refresh after whole matrix completes.

nora-cs: i'll send the playbook + bypass to their SRE and propose a canary run (2 CI runners -> 10 -> full). logging this as a renewal mitigation.

maya-ops: metrics update: after enabling TB-9212 and the customer adding 2s random jitter, 429 spike dropped 88% over the 10m window. continuing to monitor.

tomo-eng: follow-up doc action: add "CI / teardown refresh" section to quickstart with the coalesce snippet and a recommended ephemeral TTL >= 90s during onboarding. also add note to ask for `x-rw-rlimit` header when customers report 429s.

ash-se: if they can9t change CI, fallback is to extend ephemeral TTL for that account temporarily; ask CS to choose. prefer client/CI fix long-term.

nora-cs: customer ran canary under bypass and confirmed failures dropped to near zero; they implemented the jitter in CI. i'll update account health and mark renewal risk mitigated for now. reconvene if we see further anomalies.

rl-bot: bypass TB-9212 scheduled to expire automatically. metrics will be captured until expiry.

nora-cs: closing thread after final stability check at 3280012600 6 confirmed stable at +40m. captured action items for docs and onboarding checklist.
